claim: Look-ahead in the universe definition: whole-history data-quality filters decide eligibility. (1) Ten funds (BANX, CCIF, ECC, EIC, GRF, MFM, NDMO, OCCI, PDO, PEO) are dropped entirely because >1% of their rows over their WHOLE history (to 2026) contradict price/NAV (cef_data.py:112, threshold MAX_BAD_ROW_SHARE set after measuring this very data, cef_data.py:52-55); GRF, MFM and PEO have 1996-99 histories, ~2% of the 2004 universe. Their returns are not in the snapshot, so the effect cannot be measured from stored data. (2) Two funds (NRO, FXBY) are in the NAV panel but dropped from the price snapshot for an uncorroborated 2008 session (daily_data.py:212); a crude weekly price-only estimate says including them would have ADDED ~+1.9% and ~+1.0% cumulative active (vs ~107% total), so the measurable part is conservative. (3) CEFConnect's pre-2020 ZTR history does not match Yahoo's ZTR (price ratio drifts 1.76 to 0.32 to 1.00), i.e. a predecessor series is mapped onto the current ticker; ZTR was picked in 44% of sessions but contributes only ~1.3% of the active return. Net: the mechanism is real look-ahead but measured impact is small; the board should weigh (1), which is unbounded.
